title: Adequacy of Reserve Buses to Minimise Disruptions to Commuters Caught in Train Breakdowns
what_it_is: Adequacy of Reserve Buses to Minimise Disruptions to Commuters Caught in Train Breakdowns

sections.label: Reserve buses and MRT disruptions
sections.summary: Minister states reserve bus fleets are not maintained purely for train disruptions, with off-duty buses, taxi alerts and operator plans used instead.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how large is our reserve fleet of buses and drivers; (b) whether it is sufficient to minimise disruptions caused to commuters during MRT breakdowns; (c) whether there are plans to involve taxi companies and their network of taxis during such disruptions to minimise the impact on commuters; and (d) whether there is a system currently in place to hold the operators to task in cases of service disruption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It is not prudent use of resources to maintain a fleet of reserve buses and drivers to cater purely for train disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In the event of a prolonged disruption, operators will use buses that are off-duty or cross-deploy buses from less crowded services to provide bus-bridging services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Taxi companies are also alerted to inform their drivers of high demand areas along the affected routes, so that more drivers can make their vehicles available in those areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: As part of their licences, rail operators are required to have a robust Rail Incident Management Plan, which includes accurate and timely information dissemination and the provision of bus bridging services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: LTA will take regulatory action if there are failings in the implementation of this plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That when we have a prolonged disruption, we will try to ease the pain by providing free buses for bridging.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But it is never satisfactory because the bus capacity just cannot cope, especially if it happens during peak hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The moment the MRT starts to run, the queue, even though it is for free buses, just disappears.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Therefore, our priority is straightforward − focus on the basic needs, ensure train reliability.
